fixes.explanation: Yes, baker. Joshua asks why they deceived him, since they said they lived far away when they lived right there among Israel. Then he says, "Now therefore you are under a curse…" (Joshua 9:23). He means it, and the job that follows is a lasting one. I think this part is heavy.

Not a blessing, friend. Joshua says the Gibeonites are under a curse, and a lasting job comes with it. They will serve as woodcutters and water carriers for the house of his God. That's a long way from a blessing.

Spying isn't in their answer, friend. They say they were told the LORD commanded His servant Moses to give Israel all the land, and that this is why they were afraid. Fear is the reason they give, and they never mention spying.

Not what they tell Joshua, friend. They say they heard the LORD commanded His servant Moses to give Israel all the land and wipe out its inhabitants. The Gibeonites say they feared for their lives. Grabbing land never comes up in their answer.

That's the one, baker. The kings of the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites and the rest came together to wage war against Joshua and Israel. The list runs from the hill country all the way to the coast. Getting that many kings to agree on anything is a miracle. You know how a group chat can't even pick a movie?

No spies in this scene, friend. The text says the men of Israel sampled their provisions, and then Joshua made a treaty of peace with them to let them live. Nobody goes out to check the story first. The Gibeonites do say their own elders told them to go meet Israel (Joshua 9:11), but that's a different trip.
